profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company, traded as NVDA, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, USA. Its site describes the NVIDIA Nemotron family as multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, delivering agentic reasoning for graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. The company says the models are openly available with transparent training data and broad platform support, including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark, for deployment from edge to cloud.

Nemotron models are offered as optimized NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the site describes as providing peak inference performance and flexible deployment, and NIM requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license. Other tools named on the site include NVIDIA NeMo for custom agentic AI, NVIDIA Blueprints for reference workflows, NVIDIA Dynamo and TensorRT-LLM for running models at scale, and the open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. The site names NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for completing specialized tasks faster and NeMo Switchyard for routing each step to the right model. It also describes Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding, embeddings, and ranking. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is quoted on the vision behind Nemotron. The site says NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license that allows use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. ServiceNow is named among the partners working on the models.

NVIDIA's most recent 10-K, for a period ending 2026-01-25, reports revenue of $215,938,000,000. Its CIK is 0001045810. Litigation exposure is recorded in California, with 281 cases.
